title: Kadru's bet and the nagas
hook: two sisters bet on a horse's tail, a mother curses her honest snake sons, and the epic still won't make snakes the villains
carry: the nagas are honored, not hated
tomorrow: a blazing egg cracks open. who's inside?

segments.voice: Yesterday, in the Adi Parva: Ruru's stick, and a harmless snake who taught him. Ahimsa: not harming is the highest dharma.

What color is a white horse's tail? That's the bet between two sisters, Kadru and Vinata, both wives of the sage Kashyapa. They've just seen a marvelous white horse, Uchchaihshravas, which rose from the churning of the ocean. Vinata says the horse is white all over. Kadru says its tail is black. The stakes are steep: the loser becomes the winner's slave. They agree to go and look. Before they do, Kadru calls her sons. Her sons are snakes.
screen: `A WHITE HORSE FROM THE OCEAN.` → `A BET ON ITS TAIL.` → `THE LOSER BECOMES A SLAVE.`

segments.voice: Kadru tells them: go and hang on the horse's tail like black hairs, so I win. Some obey. Some refuse. And Kadru, furious, curses the ones who refuse: they will burn in the fire of a snake sacrifice held by a king named Janamejaya. That's the line the whole frame hangs on. The fire was spoken over these snakes long before Janamejaya was born. Brahma, the creator, hears the curse and lets it stand, because, the text says, the snakes had grown fierce and poisonous, a danger to others. The tail looks black, Vinata loses, and she serves her sister. And the curse fell on the innocent: the sons who said no to cheating. The text leaves that unease on the page. But a little later, the Adi Parva won't let the snakes be simple villains. They're children of a great sage, Kashyapa. Some refused to cheat. And Shesha, the eldest of them, turns from his brothers' cruelty toward Vinata, takes up austerities, and Brahma gives him a task: hold up the earth. In Hindu art, Vishnu rests on Shesha's coils on the cosmic ocean, and Shiva wears a snake at his throat. So Hindus don't only fear the nagas, the snake beings; many honor them. At Nag Panchami, families offer milk and flowers to images of the nagas and pray for protection. The same epic that builds a fire for snakes gives a snake the whole earth to carry.
screen: `THE SONS WHO REFUSE ARE CURSED.` · `BRAHMA LETS THE CURSE STAND.` · `THE CURSE FALLS ON THE INNOCENT.` · `SHESHA HOLDS UP THE EARTH.` · then, large: `THE NAGAS ARE HONORED, NOT HATED.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind a creature, or a kind of person, you've only ever seen as the threat. Now picture one of them like Kadru's sons who said no: doing the right thing at a cost. If you pray, offer that one a moment of honor, the way families offer milk and flowers to the nagas at Nag Panchami. If you don't, simply wish them well, once, on the out-breath, and let it rest.
Adi Parva. The opening book, where a mother's curse on her snake sons sets the snake sacrifice in motion.
Carry this: the nagas are honored, not hated. Even the cursed ones refused to cheat. Tomorrow: a blazing egg cracks open. That's day seven hundred.

howItsDone: At Nag Panchami, in the rainy month of Shravan, many Hindu families offer milk, flowers and turmeric to images of the nagas, drawn on walls or shaped in clay or silver, and pray for protection. In the Adi Parva, Kadru's curse is the snakes' own family story: why the fire was coming for them.

Vinata.meaning: Kadru's sister, who loses the bet and becomes her slave

sarpasatra.meaning: the snake sacrifice: the name of Janamejaya's rite

Shesha.meaning: the great snake who holds up the earth; Vishnu rests on him

naga.meaning: a snake being, honored in Hindu life
